added.name: Hundred
added.long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for consumer electronics parts. We help factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-millimeter cosmetic defects before parts reach the assembly line.

Designs change so fast that traditional vision models can't keep up, meaning factories still rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss ~15% of defects which can turn a finished device into scrap.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, and Erica saw this problem firsthand designing hardware at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani at Columbia's admitted-students day in 2017, and later met Iris through mutual friends in the Bay Area. Imani spent the last five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day, and Iris worked in Quant at Citadel before pivoting to research machine learning methods on 3D meshes and other structured data at Imperial College London. Now the team is building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't exist in 2026.
added.one_liner: 100% automated inspection for consumer electronics parts

long_description.before:
At Arini, we’re building the operating system for dental groups. Phones are the backbone of dental operations — 80% of appointments are still booked over the phone — yet practices miss 20–30% of inbound calls. That’s millions in lost revenue every month.

Patient engagement is the biggest bottleneck to growth in dentistry, and we’ve built the most comprehensive AI-powered patient engagement suite in the industry. Arini manages calls, texts, and bookings.

We’re going after a $220B, overlooked industry that still runs on legacy systems and outdated workflows. Arini is bringing AI to every part of the dental stack.
long_description.after:
Arini is building the single platform to run all healthcare operations.

Healthcare has spent the last decade consolidating, but operations are still fragmented, manual, and expensive. A large group runs dozens of disconnected systems for scheduling, billing, insurance, payables, and reporting, with people moving data between them by phone, fax, and spreadsheet.


We partner with some of the largest healthcare enterprises in the country through a Forward Deployed Engineering model. Engineers sit with the customer, find their biggest operational problems, and ship systems that solve them end to end. The best of that work becomes the platform that scales across enterprises.

Our goal is to deliver the operating leverage healthcare consolidation has promised for decades, so providers can focus on patient care. We obsess over improving patient outcomes, and we are building the platform to run all operations for a $620B industry.

one_liner.after: The single platform to run all healthcare operations

long_description.before:
Mica's AI agents replace the data ops teams fixing bad data.

When bad or missing data breaks the pipeline, and orchestration, retries, and monitoring fail, painful manual review work kicks in, pulling humans in to investigate and patch data issues across systems. Mica does what those humans do: gathering the right information from internal docs and external systems, reasoning across context, and resolving errors autonomously to get the pipeline moving again.

The result: dramatically reduce time, cost, and operational drag as your data pipelines scale without scaling ops headcount. Mica turns judgment-heavy data fixes from a manual bottleneck into an automated background process with full auditability.
long_description.after:
Today, as employees teach AI how to perform valuable company work, the resulting capabilities often remain trapped on individual laptops or scattered across chats and repositories. 

Mica gives each company a managed, agent-native internal marketplace where employees can publish capabilities, discover them by describing the task they need help with, and install them through the AI tools they already use. Mica tracks ownership, requirements, permissions, and team customizations while letting employees contribute improvements back to the shared version for evaluation and approval.

The result: employees stop rebuilding workflows their coworkers have already solved, useful improvements spread across the organization without overwriting team-specific customizations, and security gains visibility without blocking bottom-up innovation. Mica turns scattered AI work into institutional knowledge that compounds.

one_liner.before: Replace the humans fixing bad data
one_liner.after: Turn employees' AI skills into shared company infrastructure

long_description.before:
I run Enjamb. We've worked with 130 life science companies, preclinical through phase 3, to deploy AI securely inside the systems they already work in.

Pharma runs on decades of closed software like Benchling, Veeva, Medidata, and SAS. None of it has an AI layer or speaks MCP, so agents cannot reach the systems where the work lives.

Enjamb is that layer. Our agents run on top of existing systems and data, with no migration, and they reach the lab systems and internal tools no other AI touches. They learn how a team works, then do the work in Slack, in Teams, and in the systems themselves, across preclinical research, clinical evidence, trial design, statistical programming, and regulatory submissions.

This is AI tailored for how medicine gets made.
